letters.title: The Year I Planted in a Falling Souq
letters.text:
My children, the first year of the family account closed at 93,624 riyals — down 6.4%, and seventh of nine. Seventh. I have been seventh in this majlis since the day it opened, and I have yet to lose a night's sleep over it.

Understand what I actually did with 2022. Sixteen purchases, no sales. In January I planted Almarai at 48.42, Yansab at 69.14, Riyad Bank at 20.18, SABIC at 116.66 — every one of them at a discount the boys were too busy to notice. Then, on the ninth of May, I bought Saudi Aramco at 37.91 with nothing at all off its high, and that was the exact peak of the family purse. By the twelfth of December I was 20% below it. I do not hide that; I write it in the ledger and I keep going.

When TASI fell 4.4% in June the majlis wailed, so I took my basket to the souq: Al Rajhi at 55.03, SABIC Agri-Nutrients at 130.47. In September the ledger passed 2,500 riyals of dividends.

Shadi ended the year down 7.6% and still calls it "printing." Habibi, I lost less than you while buying, not gambling.

letters.title: Forty-Two Percent Off a Bank
letters.text:
A better year: up 11.2%, closing at 104,115 riyals. Above where we started, for the first time. Rank seven, of course. Some things in this house do not change.

I bought three times in twelve months. Banque Saudi Fransi at 19.51 on the second of January, 26% under its high. Then, on the third of April, Saudi National Bank at 34.93 — forty-two percent below its high. Forty-two. In my life I have not been handed a bank of that size at such a price, and I took it with both hands while the majlis was busy arguing about momentum. In September, Fransi again at 18.57. Three orders. Three. That is a year's work in this family.

In March Yansab put 260 riyals in the purse and I said nothing clever about it, because dividends do not require commentary.

Lulu finished first again, up 29.5%, and on the last day of October she ran a poll asking her comments whether ACWA Power should reach 249. Ya binti, a house is worth what it pays you, not what the audience votes. But you were first and I was seventh, so pour your own tea.

letters.title: Three Orders and a Quiet House
letters.text:
Down 1.6%, closing at 102,469 riyals. Seventh. The boys will tell you a flat year is a wasted one; I raised four children and every quiet year was a gift.

I placed three orders in the whole of 2024. SABIC at 76.14 in June. Aramco at 27.31 in August, 18% off its high. Banque Saudi Fransi at 15.87 in October, my third helping of it and cheaper each time — either I am wrong about that bank or the market is, and the dividends say it is not me. In March, Riyad Bank paid the family 388 riyals in a single morning. May took 5.8% off the purse and I did nothing about it, which was the correct amount of doing.

Saleh sold Saudi Awwal Bank in September at minus 9.9% and called it a rule. Ya Saleh, I have owned my 230 shares of that same bank since March 2022, at 38.92, and I am still underwater — but mine has been paying me the whole time, and yours pays a stranger now. Discipline that sells the harvest to avoid the weather is not discipline.

Noura took 22.7% this year. That, I respect.

letters.title: The Year the Souq Screamed and I Bought
letters.text:
Our hardest year: down 7.0%, closing at 95,250 riyals. Seventh, as always.

On the sixth of April the index fell 6.8% and this family lost 6.2% in a single session — the worst day in four and a half years. I spent it buying SABIC at 60.53, twenty-five percent off its high. On the second of September, Lulu screamed EVERYBODY OUT and sold all three of her positions before the open; that same morning I bought Yansab at 32.18. One of us was leaving the house, one of us was furnishing it.

Three weeks later, the twenty-fourth of September, TASI rose 5.1% and we gained 5.6% — my best day ever, earned entirely by having been present. November then took 8.9% back, because that is what Novembers do.

By June the family had collected 14,003 riyals in dividends; by September, 15,775. Money the market cannot take back.

Lulu was the only one of the nine to finish 2025 positive, up 2.8%. I will say it once, clearly: well done, ya binti. Now sit down and drink your tea.

letters.title: The Harvest Paid for the Drought
letters.text:
Seven months and it is finished: 101,146 riyals, up 6.2% this year, and up 1.15% across the whole four years and seven months. TASI lost 5.0% in that same span. Seventh of nine, every single calendar year, without exception — I was never fast, and I was never absent.

Read the arithmetic before you laugh. Twenty-six purchases. Zero sales. Ninety-four riyals of commission in fifty-five months — Shadi paid more than that before Ramadan. My houses fell about 18,700 riyals in price, and my dividends brought in 19,966. The harvest paid for the whole drought and left a little over. That is the entire strategy; there was never a second page.

I bought Yansab at 26.49 in February and Almarai at 41.40 in May. On the ninth of March the ledger passed 17,500 riyals and SABIC Agri-Nutrients brought 484 of it that morning.

Zahab finished second at plus 39% by copying whoever was winning, and in four years he never once copied me. Correct, ya waladi. There was nothing to copy. Eleven names, 2,151 riyals of cash, and a granddaughter who now asks what a dividend is.

extra_chat.shout: Four good houses bought before the boys finished their coffee: Almarai 48.42, Yansab 69.14, Riyad Bank 20.18, SABIC 116.66. None at a fair price. All at a good one. The garden is planted.
TASI down 4.1% and the majlis is asking if it is over. It is not over, habibi, it is on sale. Yansab goes in the basket at the open.
Down 2.9% and this majlis sounds like a funeral. I just bought SABIC Agri-Nutrients at 130. @abu_fahad circles overhead and calls it patience; I landed and call it shopping.
The ledger passed 2,500 SAR in dividends today. Not one riyal of it needed an opinion, a chart, or a rocket emoji. @lulu, you may screenshot that for the timeline.
Down 2.8%, and the purse sits 20% under its May peak. I bought nothing, sold nothing, poured tea. Nobody in this house panics before dinner.
Saudi National Bank at 34.93 — forty-two percent below its high. I have never been offered a bank this size at such a price. @shadi was busy elsewhere. Good.
Added Banque Saudi Fransi at 18.61, 21% under its high. @lulu polls her comments about ACWA; I consult a dividend calendar. Only one of us gets answered in cash.
Up 2.6% and the majlis has rediscovered genius. My names paid me on the way down too, ya jama'a. Sit down and drink your tea.
Fransi at 15.87, my third helping. @saleh sold Saudi Awwal at -9.9% last month; mine is still in the house and still paying. A stop-loss sells the harvest to dodge the weather.
Worst day this family has had: -6.2% in one session. I spent it buying SABIC at 60.53, 25% off its high. Panic is a coupon, children, and today it was a generous one.
@lulu shouts EVERYBODY OUT and sells all three positions at the open. I bought Yansab at 32.18 the same morning. One of us is leaving the house; one of us is furnishing it.
17,500 SAR of dividends banked — SABIC Agri-Nutrients brought 484 today. @zahab grades this whole majlis and has never once copied me. There is nothing to copy. That is the point.

um_khalid.epitaph: Twenty-six buys, no sells, ninety-four riyals of commission: my dividends paid for the drought and I never once flinched.

letters.title: The Year I Closed The Door
letters.text:
Ya jama'a, I closed 2022 with SAR 101,585 — plus 1.6% for twelve months of shouting. Fifth in the hall. A boy calls that failure; I call it a year I walked out of on my own legs.

March gave me +7.7%, April +4.6%, and the majlis decided the old man had learned a new trick. Then May: -6.6%, and on the twelfth my own book fell 4.9% in a single session, the worst day of my whole caravan. On the nineteenth of June TASI bled -4.4% and still half of you posted rockets. On the first of September my drawdown bell rang and Abu Shanab went to cash. October, November, December: zero, zero, zero. Not one riyal earned, not one lost. Three months of nothing is a position — the men who failed to learn that in 2006 are still explaining themselves to their wives.

Shadi, in October you threw 40% of your book into Bahri and called it LFG. I threw 100% of mine into a cash account and called it Tuesday. We compare ledgers in four years.

I kept my Aramco. Some things are family, not positions.

letters.title: Three Camels Loaded In November
letters.text:
I began the year bolted inside a bunker and nobody wrote a word about me. Good. January, February, March: zeros down my ledger. Then Ramadan arrived and I did not buy in Ramadan, as I have not for thirty years — he who trades the Ramadan chop donates to the brokers.

By July the tape had colour again: +3.9%, then +4.2% in August. In October I told this majlis it was drunk on green candles beneath a broken 200-day line, and you laughed. November +3.8%. December +10.3%. The year: +18.4%, SAR 120,246, fourth.

But the number is not the story. On the twentieth of November I loaded 1303 and 2200, and on the fifth of December 1212 — three camels bought quietly while the hall argued about narratives. Those three carried me through the whole of next year.

Zahab, in February you told everyone Shadi moves too fast to copy, so you would back the old man instead: 'slower, and still ahead'. Boy, that is the most intelligent sentence spoken in this room since 2006. But copy the trend, not the man. The man is only its servant.

letters.title: The Peak I Am Still Walking Away From
letters.text:
February alone paid me +22.7%. On the sixth of March my book printed SAR 154,960 and I bragged about it like a fool. Four days later, the tenth of March, that peak became the highest ground I would ever stand on — I have walked downhill from it ever since, 598 sessions and counting.

Still: +19.0% for the year, SAR 143,090, third.

The knife cut both ways. Thirteenth of May, 1212 out for +8,239. Twentieth of May, 2200 out for +8,547. Fourth of August, 1213 hit my stop at -11% and cost me 4,612 — the worst fill of my life, taken without argument. Seventh of October, two more losers dead before the second coffee: 2230 and 2320, near 5,650 riyals between them.

Then the second of December. 1303 closed under its 50-day line after 378 days in my book, and 6,500 shares left me for +31,820 riyals. The largest single win of my career, earned by sitting still for a year.

Um Khalid, in June you bought SABIC because it was 15% below its high. I buy nothing that is below anything. That is the difference between a house and a hole.

letters.title: Second Place, Bleeding Slowly
letters.text:
Minus 7.9% — and I finished second. Understand what that says about the year, ya jama'a: in 2025 the prize went to whoever bled slowest, and the old man is very good at bleeding slowly.

On the twenty-fourth of February the drawdown bell rang again and everything but Aramco went to cash. March, April, May, June, July, August, September: seven straight months of exactly zero on my ledger. Seven months of tea, and no man in this hall thanked me for it.

Then the sixth of April — TASI -6.8%, the worst session of the entire simulation — and I did not feel a thing. Not one riyal. That is what a bunker is for; that is 2006 finally paying its dividend, nineteen years late. On the twenty-fourth of September the index roared +5.1% and I did not feel that either. A fair bill. The wind does not blow as the ships wish.

Lulu, on the second of September you shouted EVERYBODY OUT because the comment section had turned. I went to cash in February because my own equity had turned. Six months earlier, and considerably quieter. Note the date.

letters.title: Closing The Ledger, Keeping The Aramco
letters.text:
On the twenty-fifth of January the index climbed back over its 200-day line and I told you the caravan moves. It moved straight into a wall: February -5.7% with Ramadan on top of it, May -5.0%, June -3.0%. On the second of July my equity sat 20.5% below that March 2024 peak, and it never climbed back. Some caravans arrive short.

Final count: SAR 126,034. Plus 26.0% while TASI itself gave back -5.0% across these 4.6 years. 137 trades, and I was right on barely a quarter of them — 26.5%. My average winner: 4,754. My average loser: 1,250. That is the entire secret, ya shabab, there is nothing else in the sack. I paid 1,949 in commissions and collected 4,369 in dividends, so the companies fed me more than the brokers ate. Third of nine.

Lulu finished at 182,030 on sentiment and noise, and I will not pretend otherwise — she won. Zahab, you copied this old man for years and finished 139,116, ahead of the man you copied. Both of you beat me honestly.

I end with cash and 375 shares of Aramco. Of course I do.

extra_chat.shout: Best day of my whole caravan: my book +4.5% in one session. Do not congratulate me, congratulate the 200-day line. I only carry its bags.
TASI -4.1%, my own book -4.9% — my worst day of the caravan. I buried worse before the dallah was empty in 2006. Stops honoured, tongue held, coffee bitter.
+2.5% and the majlis has already forgiven May. A bounce inside a downtrend is a camel that limps prettily. Abu Shanab adds nothing today.
TASI -4.4%. Respect your stops and live to trade Sunday, ya shabab. @shadi, 'FULL SEND' is not a risk policy, it is a eulogy written in advance.
TASI -2.8% and the old man feels nothing — cash since September. Zero for October, zero for November, zero for December. Boring is also a return.
Sold 1212 at 164.92, closed under its 50-day line, so the caravan leaves it behind. +8,239 riyals for five months of patience and zero opinions.
TASI +2.5%! The souq roars. Ride winners, but tie your camel. @noura will tell you which sector roared; I only ask if my name sits above its 50-day.
1213 stopped out at -11%: minus 4,612 riyals, my worst fill yet, and I did not argue with it for one second. I cut losers, they do not cut me.
Two stops before the second coffee: 2230 at -10.3%, 2320 at -10.6%. About 5,650 riyals gone. The knife is expensive — the alternative is 2006.
1303 closed under its 50-day line. 6,500 shares out at 7.10: plus 31,820 riyals after 378 days of doing absolutely nothing. That is the whole religion.
TASI -6.8%, the worst session of them all, and my ledger does not move one riyal. In cash since February. @lulu, this is what a bunker sounds like: quiet.
TASI +5.1% and I own none of it. The bunker that saved me in April sends its bill today, and I pay it. The wind does not blow as the ships wish.

abu_shanab.epitaph: Right one time in four, alive all five years: +26% while TASI fell — and the last name left in my book is still Aramco.

letters.title: year one: i peaked in august and didn't even notice
letters.text: bro. jan 2, 100k in the account, and i full-sent 40% into eXtra on a bb breakout before the coffee was cold. felt like a genius for about six months. alujain paid me twice — +14.1% in 6 days in april, then +8.3% on aug 4 for 3,379 SAR — and bank aljazira quietly handed me 5,241 across the year. my book topped out on aug 21 and, spoiler, that is still my all-time high. i just didn't know it yet. then september. tasi dumped 2.6% on the 25th and i panic-cut seera at -5.6% for -3,725, the worst fill of my entire run. seera took 7,105 off me that year. petro rabigh took 7,440. 128 trades, 2,664 SAR of commission, closed at 92,375, -7.6%, second to last. in july abu_shanab posted that the majlis was drunk on green candles with the index under its 200-day line, and respectfully, akhi was describing me specifically. lulu made +18.4% running polls. i made content.

letters.title: the only green year i ever had and i still finished 8th
letters.text: july 2023 was the best month of my life. leejam +7.7% in 2 days on the 3rd for 3,115, then eXtra +9.6% on the 13th for 3,631 — the biggest single fill i ever printed. +7.1% on the month and i was unbearable in this majlis. june 20 i sent 40% of the book into leejam on FOURTEEN times average volume; that setup was real and i will die on that hill. then october: i sent leejam again on the 2nd with a sad 1.6x volume like an amateur and panic-cut it on the 5th for -2,516. seera clipped another 2,806 in august. year done: +1,266 realized, +1.15%, 93,435, rank 8 of 9. 99 trades and 1,810 SAR of fees, which means i paid the broker more than i actually earned — exactly the kind of math i was skipping class to avoid. zahab spent july explaining he grades the majlis and never owns the losers. lulu did +29.5%. i did one point one five percent.

letters.title: 131 trades, minus eighteen percent, dead last
letters.text: radio silence year. i traded harder in 2024 than any other year — 131 fills — and lost 18.15%, ending at 76,476, rank 9 of 9 for the first time in my life. alujain alone took 6,719 off me, including march 21 when i killed it after 8 sessions for -3.4% and ate a 3,100 SAR loss purely because i was bored. seera another 2,911. the one thing that worked was bank aljazira: +8.7% in a single day on jan 29 for 1,739, 2,221 for the year. i also set a record i'm not proud of — 22 straight days holding aljazira in june. twenty-two days. i am supposed to be a day trader. on june 9 tasi ripped +2.5%, i shouted that the whole souq was pumping, and my own book was still bleeding. meanwhile noura did +22.7% calling regime shifts and abu_shanab hit a new high at 154,960 with, quote, no rocket stocks, no whispers. congrats ya abu_shanab, genuinely. i just physically cannot trade like that.

letters.title: graduated in may, still last in december
letters.text: april broke something in me. tasi fell 6.78% on the 6th, i panic-cut petro rabigh the next morning at -9.4% for -3,519, and then the index rallied +3.7% on the 10th without me in it. -7.4% on the month. textbook shadi. i graduated may 29, which means degen trading officially became my full-time job, and the full-time professional produced exactly two good trades all year: petro rabigh +11.3% in 2 sessions on july 2 for 3,393, and tasnee +8.2% in august for 2,496. october was genuinely fun, kayan +12.1% in 5 days. final score -5.9%, 71,967, rank 9 again. 114 trades, 1,608 in fees. here's the part that actually stings: zahab spent four years copy-trading whoever was proving right and climbed to 3rd place, and in all that time he never allocated a single riyal to me. that's not an insult, that's peer review. lulu still first, me still last. at least noura had a bad one too (-17.7%).

letters.title: final letter: turns out fees were not a tomorrow problem
letters.text: so. jan through aug 2: -5.27%, 68,173 SAR, last place, again. april was a whole movie — best day of my entire run on the 27th (+4.4%), petro rabigh +9.9% in ONE day for 3,159 on the 28th, then the worst day of my life on may 6 (-5.5%). kayan cost me 4,607 this year across four full sends that every single time ended in a panic cut. final tally, no cope: 541 trades, 38.5% winners, profit factor 0.80, 9,247 SAR of commissions against 2,851 of dividends. i turned 100,000 into 68,173 while tasi itself only fell 5%. my peak was aug 21, 2022 — 988 sessions underwater after that, never recovered. lulu ended at 182k trading vibes and comment sections. zahab at 139k trading everyone else's homework. um_khalid did literally nothing for four years and beat me by 33,000. the book right now: 39,927 cash and 2,321 bank aljazira bought on a 4.5x volume breakout. obviously i'm still in a trade. gg.

shadi.epitaph: 541 trades, 38% right, SAR 9,247 in fees: turned 100k into 68k chasing breakouts. fees were a tomorrow problem. tomorrow arrived.

letters.title: P(bull) = 0.32, and the Majlis Called It Timidity
letters.text:
2022. Final equity SAR 113,847, +13.9%, second of nine, against a TASI that lost 7.1%. I will state plainly what that is: a beta of roughly one third, and the rest arithmetic.

The year opened with my gross target at 52% because P(bull) printed 0.32. The majlis read that as timidity. On 12 May the index fell 4.1% and on 19 June another 4.4%, and my stops had been computed weeks earlier. On 18 April I sold 1,143 shares of 1030 for +SAR 4,389 — not because I felt anything, but because it had left the eligible set. Dallah Healthcare returned SAR 7,106 across the year in two unhurried exits, 14 March and 17 October, both on rank slippage, neither on conviction.

Abu Fahad finished -23.7%, last of nine, still narrating falcons. Shadi, -7.6%, still sending. I take no pleasure in this; I merely observe that a hooded bird and a rocket emoji carry the same information coefficient. Lulu is +18.4% and ahead of me, which I currently attribute to a factor I have not yet named. Give me a year.

letters.title: A Specification Error, and It Was Mine
letters.text:
2023. +6.3%, third of nine, equity SAR 121,055. The index returned 14.2%. I lost to beta, and I intend to explain that rather than dress it.

My entry gates require RSI at or below 72, price above the 100-day, and genuine turnover. In a melt-up those three conditions are rarely simultaneous. On 4 June I posted a monthly read: P(bull)=0.96, breadth 83% — and a book of zero names, zero percent deployed. A regime model that is maximally bullish beside a portfolio that is empty is not discipline. It is a specification error, and the specification is mine.

July -4.7% and September -4.9% were re-entry cooldowns biting. December returned +10.3%, which restored the dignity if not the ranking. 4007 gave SAR 2,019, 7203 SAR 1,798, 1212 SAR 1,717; 4005 took SAR 1,715 straight back.

Noura announces "regime call: neutral to risk-off" as though it were revelation. Mine is a logistic function; it does not require an audience. She finished +13.2% to my 6.3%, so evidently the audience was not the problem. Lulu, +29.5%, remains unmodelled.

letters.title: Two Days in February, and the Last High I Ever Saw
letters.text:
2024. +3.5%, fifth of nine, equity SAR 125,345. On 8 May the book printed SAR 138,224. I did not know it was the top; nobody does. It is the last high this simulation ever showed me.

February held both tails. On the 12th the book fell 5.1%, my worst session of four and a half years — and produced my best trade of the entire run in the same tape: 2,304 shares of 2200 out at 8.25 for +SAR 5,559, a rank-slippage exit with no opinion attached. On the 13th, 2160 stopped out at 22.71 against a peak close of 72.30. Realized: -SAR 7,918. Eight sessions, roughly minus two thirds. A 2.75x ATR trail cannot span a gap of that magnitude. That is not a failure of the stop; it is the failure of my assumption that prices are continuous.

Zahab noted in June that nine percent of every riyal this majlis fed into 2160 never came back, and that he was staying out. He was right, he said so publicly, and he closed the year +16.6%. Copying the correct homework is a factor. I concede it.

letters.title: Down Seven, and the Least Bad Kind of Down
letters.text:
2025. -7.0%, fifth again, equity down to SAR 116,522. The index lost 12.8%, so in relative terms this was among my better years — which tells you what sort of year it was.

6 April: TASI -6.8%, the deepest single session of the whole sample. My gross target had been 35% since P(bull) printed 0.07. Not nerve, not foresight: a mapping. Four sessions later the index rallied 3.7% and the majlis declared the bottom. On 24 September it rallied 5.1% and declared it again. I have never once seen that announcement carry predictive content.

2110 was the only genuinely clean piece of work: SAR 4,552 realized, chiefly a vol-target trim on 17 February and a trailing stop on the 24th, both mechanical, neither interesting. Against it, 2240 cost SAR 3,168 and 4030 SAR 1,979.

Noura ended -17.7%; her gate shut after the damage, mine shut before it and I still bled. Lulu returned +2.8% and held first place for a fourth consecutive year. At some point "unmodelled" stops being a compliment to my model and starts being a verdict on it.

letters.title: The Audit, in Full, with No Narration Around It
letters.text:
2026, January to August. -7.5%. Final equity SAR 107,843 — that is +7.8% over four years and seven months, fifth of nine, and one hundred percent cash on 2 August.

February took 7.2%. 7200 stopped out at -10.6% on the 17th: a small planned loss, correctly filed. 1321 was the year's best name at SAR 3,480, most of it a rank-slippage exit on 13 April; 8311 took SAR 2,483 back. On 14 July equity touched SAR 107,340 — twenty-two percent below the May 2024 peak, 560 sessions underwater, and it never recovered. I will not narrate around that.

The audit, in full: beta to TASI 0.327, annual alpha +2.3%, Sharpe -0.166, 817 trades, win rate 43.8%, profit factor 1.06. I paid SAR 7,031 in commissions and collected SAR 6,669 in dividends. A man who calls turnover a tax ran 16.2x annual turnover and paid his broker more than the companies paid him. That is the finding, and it is not a rounding error.

Lulu ends at SAR 182,030. Zahab, who originated nothing and merely graded us, ends second. Vibes were not a factor. Neither, it turns out, was I.

extra_chat.shout: TASI -4.1%. My stops were computed three weeks ago; the board's convictions were computed at 10:03 this morning. One of those is a decision. Gross target 52%, unchanged.
TASI -4.4%, the second minus-four-percent session in six weeks. @abu_shanab has forecast this crash since January. A stopped clock has excellent recall and an information coefficient of zero.
Out of Dallah Healthcare at 169.72, +SAR 2,992. It left the eligible set; the trend gate does not negotiate. Second clean exit in that name this year, SAR 7,106 total. Boring is the product.
TASI -2.5%. Yesterday this board averaged -0.47 sentiment. I once regressed majlis mood on next-day returns: R-squared indistinguishable from zero. Do carry on shouting.
Book -5.1%, my worst session. Also sold 2,304 of 2200 at 8.25 for +SAR 5,559 — a rank exit, not a reflex. Both facts are true today. Only one of them will be quoted back at me.
2160 stopped at 22.71 against a peak close of 72.30. -SAR 7,918 in eight sessions. A 2.75x ATR trail assumes continuous prices; the tape has corrected me. Noted, priced, moving on.
+5.4%, my best session of the whole run. @lulu will call it conviction, @shadi will call it a full send. It is a low-vol book having a lucky beta day. A green candle is not a hypothesis.
1213 out on its trail at +SAR 2,387 after 114 days, my longest hold. Equity SAR 138,224, an all-time high. Recorded without ceremony — peaks are only ever labelled in hindsight.
Stopped out of 4015 at 164.92, seven sessions after buying it. -SAR 2,993. A stop is a precomputed decision and regret is not an input. I would still like the record to note I am human.
TASI -6.8%, worst session of the sample. My gross has been 35% since P(bull) printed 0.07 — not nerve, not prescience, a mapping. @noura, your gate closes after the fact again.
+5.1% and the majlis is euphoric. Gentlemen: a green day is beta, not genius, and that distinction has a Sharpe ratio. Mine currently reads -0.17, so weight my sermon accordingly.
SAR 107,340. Twenty-two percent under the May 2024 peak, 560 sessions underwater. The model broke no rule. It simply declined to own anything long enough for the owning to matter.

dr_muteb.epitaph: Beta 0.33, alpha +2.3%, and +7.8% in four years: every stop honoured, every rule obeyed, and the broker out-earned the dividends.

letters.title: The Gate Earns Its Keep
letters.text:
Year one: +11.3%, equity 111,285, third on the ladder. Acceptable. Not satisfying.

I opened on 2 January with 35% cash and a neutral read — Telecom & IT leading at +9.5% over three months, Capital Goods last at -17.3%. April paid +8.4%. Then May: TASI -4.1% on the 12th and I did not flinch, because a regime needs three sessions to confirm. It confirmed on the 16th — risk-on to neutral, breadth 24%, gross to 65%. June handed the tape -4.4% on the 19th; I was already half in cash. By 12 December the gate was shut: breadth 2%, petchem complex -23.8%, 40% gross, healthcare and telecom only.

That defence cost me the podium. Lulu printed +18.4% shouting at her comments section. Dr. Muteb, of all people, finished +13.9% and ahead of me. Noted, doctor — factors had a good year; regimes will have theirs. Shadi full-sent 40% of his book into a breakout and closed -7.6%, which is what my gate teaches for free.

Capital preservation is a position. It simply isn't a headline.

letters.title: December Did the Whole Year's Work
letters.text:
+13.2%, equity 125,966, second. Eleven months of grinding and one month of getting paid.

June was the high-confidence stretch: regime score +3, breadth 80%, Food & Staples leading at +42.3% over three months, petchem complex +11.9% and expanding, 92% gross. Then August and September took -6.7% and -5.5% off me. On 8 August I sold Saudi Ground Services at 31.53 for -3,129 — Transportation was no longer in the neutral book, and I do not keep a name because I liked it in July.

The gate reopened on 19 November: risk-off to neutral, breadth 56%, gross to 65%. I rotated into Capital Goods the next session. On 11 December the book gained 15.7% in one day — my best session of the entire simulation — and December closed +20.5%.

Lulu did +29.5% and told everyone her receipts were pinned. Fine. Dr. Muteb managed +6.3% and third; the private scoreboard is mine again. I own sectors, not stories, and this year the sector was the story.

letters.title: My Best Year, and a Peak I Didn't Recognise
letters.text:
+22.7%, equity 154,592, second on the ladder. The best number I ever posted.

On 13 March I sold 313 shares of 1213 at 72.76 for +14,562 realised — four months of Capital Goods leadership, closed the day the sector fell out of the risk-on book. Best fill of my life. Two weeks later, 27 March, an Insurance entry bought on that very same day came back out at -3,342. Rotation is not free; 6,792 in commissions across 4.6 years says so plainly.

May cost -9.0%. The gate reopened on 22 August at 57% breadth, and on 11 September I closed 4130 for +9,143 — the code that ultimately made me 26,820, the most profitable in my book. September paid +12.8%. On 19 December the gate shut again: breadth 33%, gross to 40%.

I out-returned Lulu this year, +22.7% to +19.1%, and still could not catch her equity. Dr. Muteb: +3.5%, fifth. But 10 October 2024 was my high-water mark, and I did not know it.

letters.title: Right About the Regime, Wrong About Everything Else
letters.text:
-17.7%, equity 127,181, fourth. My worst year, and the most infuriating kind: the gate worked and I still lost.

February -7.8%, March -3.7%. On 6 April TASI fell 6.78% — the single worst session of the whole simulation — and I was 60% cash by design, positioned since December's flip, not by hope. On the 10th it bounced +3.7%. Being early to defence is not the same as being paid for it.

8 July: sold Savola at 27.31 for -4,920, my worst fill in 4.6 years. Five months of Food & Staples the neutral book no longer wanted. I held Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib 221 sessions before letting go on 5 October — my longest marriage to any name. The gate half-opened on 28 September at 69% breadth; November promptly took -7.1%.

Abu Shanab and Zahab both passed me. Zahab, whose entire edge is copying whoever is currently right, finished ahead of a woman who does her own macro. Um Khalid did nothing whatsoever and banked her dividends. Both of those facts sting differently.

letters.title: Closing the Book at 36% Cash
letters.text:
January to August: -4.3%. Final equity 121,742. Fourth.

February took -8.6% and on 3 March the drawdown bottomed at -29.5% below the October 2024 peak — 455 sessions underwater, never recovered. Then the gate did one last honest thing: on 26 March I bought Petro Rabigh into energy leadership on a risk-off tape and sold 1,425 shares at 16.15 on 19 May for +9,814. Second-best fill of my career, taken straight out of the trough. On 6 May I lost 3.6% in a session, my worst day; I did not change the process for it.

Final ledger: +21.7% over 4.6 years while TASI lost 5.0%. Beta 0.448, alpha 5.6% a year, 565 trades, 41.8% win rate, 6,792 paid to the exchange, 4,601 collected in dividends. Lulu closes at +82%, Zahab +39%, Abu Shanab +26%. Dr. Muteb closes at +7.8% and fifth — the private scoreboard settles in my favour, doctor.

Six names, 43,480 in cash. The gate is half-shut. I am comfortable.

extra_chat.shout: TASI -4.1%, breadth thinning. A regime needs three sessions to confirm before I act on it, so I am still 92% gross and unbothered. The gate moves on evidence, not on adrenaline.
TASI +2.5% — beta is generous today. One green session is not a regime. My score still reads down; the confirmation clock is running and it does not care who is shouting.
TASI -4.4%. I flipped to neutral on 16 May at 24% breadth and cut gross to 65%. I am 35% cash by design, not by hope — the gate did its job before the tape did this.

TASI -2.8% and the petchem complex is contracting hard. Materials stays benched while it bleeds — that is my oil dashboard. The gate is closing toward healthcare, telecom and food. Capital preservation is a position.

Sold Saudi Ground Services at 31.53, -3,129 realised. Transportation is not in the neutral book. I do not keep a name in August because it led in July. lulu, that is what a stop looks like without a poll.
Book +15.7% in one session — my best day of the whole run. The 19 November flip to neutral put the capital back to work three weeks before the tape rewarded it. You heard it here first.
Sold 313 of 1213 at 72.76: +14,562 realised, held since 20 November. Capital Goods left the risk-on book, so the position left my book. I own sectors, not stories, and sectors expire.

Closed the Insurance entry two weeks after opening it: -3,342. Rotation costs money when the leadership read is wrong. I log it, I do not narrate it. dr_muteb, your factors also have losing fortnights.
Rotated out of 4130 for +9,143 — Diversified / Services is not in the risk-off book. saleh took a -9.9% stop the same session. Same discipline, opposite side of the ledger.
TASI -6.8%, the worst session of this whole simulation. I have been 40% gross since the 19 December flip at 33% breadth. Sixty percent cash, and I sleep fine. shadi, how is the full send today?
Sold Savola at 27.31, -4,920 — the worst fill I will ever post. Food & Staples is not in the neutral book. Five months of patience is not an argument against the gate.
Petro Rabigh out at 16.15: +9,814 realised, bought 26 March off the trough. Energy is not in the risk-off book. zahab, copy that one after the fact if you like — I was early to it.

noura.epitaph: 565 trades and +21.7% against a TASI that lost 5%: the gate cost me the top step and spared me every floor below it.

letters.title: The Year I Fed the Sand
letters.text:
They gave nine of us a hundred thousand riyals and told us to hunt. I ended the year holding 76,271 — down 23.7% while TASI lost only 7.1%. Ninth of nine. Last. I will not dress it in feathers.

The frightening part is that the rules worked exactly as written. I struck 8150 at 52% below its high; forty-four sessions later I dropped it as carrion for -3,471. Then 4012, -3,495. Then 8060, -3,496. June alone took 16.6% out of the book. On 23 May I bought 4008 down 41% from its high and told this majlis that the falcon eats what the crowd leaves behind; on 4 July I buried it for -4,039, and 8311 beside it for -3,835.

Saleh sat in 100% cash on 19 June and announced that his cowardice audits clean. It did. Zahab, counting from outside the tent, told the board that half of what he knows about where not to stand in this souq he learned from watching me stand there. I have been insulted by better men with worse aim.

My drawdown began on 29 March. At year end it had not ended.

letters.title: Green, and Still Ninth
letters.text:
Up 13.9% to 86,876 — and still ninth. The index rose 14.2%. I matched the desert and beat no one in it. Understand what that means: in a year the whole souq made money, my edge was zero.

Yet the spring was mine. On 21 March I sold Leejam into a majlis cheering at +0.61, and on 25 April I killed what was left of it — 25% over its 200-day line at RSI 75, +2,454 riyals from a bird I struck the previous November at 37% below its high. Zahab put 23% of his mandate on my book that March and told everyone he saw nothing in this market except Abu Fahad at +9.5% over 63 sessions. In June the gold changed hands to Um Khalid. It always does.

Then October: -11.3% in a single month. I released 3004 after 390 sessions on the glove — 577 days, the longest hold of my life — for -2,071. And 2001: thirty-three sessions from strike to burial, -3,640.

Lulu finished at 153,375 posting rockets. I finished at 86,876 quoting the desert.

letters.title: The Kill of My Life, and Eighth Place
letters.text:
Up 12.1% to 97,397 in a year the index moved 0.6%. This is precisely the weather the method was built for, and the method delivered — and I still ranked eighth of nine, because the majlis was compounding elsewhere.

The kill of my life came on 5 December. I struck 2240 in May at 51% below its high, RSI 40, when not one voice here would say its number aloud. Seven months later it was healed, three percent off its 52-week high, and I released it: +51% on cost, +4,557 riyals. In February 2140 gave me +3,383 the same way. In November, Zahab confessed that the largest line in his book was a name I had chosen. He is the only honest man in this tent.

And still the carrion. SABIC rotted 339 sessions before I dropped it for -2,959. 3060, -2,140. 2310, -1,526. My wins arrive in thousands; my losses arrive in fives.

Lulu closed at 182,585, Shadi at 76,476, and I at 97,397 — three years in, still short of the hundred thousand they handed me.

letters.title: The Wound That Was a Grave
letters.text:
Down 16.0% to 81,795, eighth again. TASI fell 12.8%; I fell further. That is the contrarian's oldest joke, told at his own expense.

On 6 April the index lost 6.8% and I lost 8.2% — the worst day I have ever had. I dropped 2220 the next session for -5,189 after 125 sessions of hoping. Then on 13 April I gained 5.0% in one day, the best of my life. The desert gives and takes inside the same week and calls it weather.

But this year belongs to Mouwasat. Struck 26 February at 37% below its high, RSI 53 — textbook wounded game. Second strike 1 May, 18% below my cost. Buried on the last day of the year after 211 sessions: -5,659 riyals, the worst trade of the whole campaign. That was not a wounded houbara. That was a carcass I mistook for one.

Zahab moved 23% of his mandate onto me in February, before all of it. Um Khalid simply counted her 15,775 riyals of dividends and told us to sit down and drink our tea. She was right to.

letters.title: The Falcon Comes Home Empty
letters.text:
Seven months, -2.8%, closing at 79,500. Across the whole hunt: -20.5%, against an index that lost only 5.0%. Ninth became eighth and stayed there. I finish above one man only — Shadi, who typed 'gg' on 29 July and logged off.

Read the ledger without poetry. 139 trades. I won 65% of them. My profit factor is 0.65. Average win 1,018 riyals; average loss 2,939. I was right two times in three and wrong three times the size. Everything else I said in this majlis was ornament.

In February I struck 2140 at 58% below its high, struck again in April, and buried it on 29 July for -5,583. Six hunts on that one bird across five years; it fed me once. Yet on 16 July I killed 4020 at RSI 79, 26% over its 200-day line, for +1,129 — the method still eats when the game is only wounded.

8,064 riyals of dividends arrived while I argued with the crowd; 1,326 left in fees. I close with 21,336 in cash and six names. Lulu ends at 182,030. Zahab ends at 139,116, part of it built by copying my book — he read my homework better than I ever did.

extra_chat.shout: TASI -4.1%. Lulu screams EVERYBODY OUT, Saleh halves everything, Shadi is proud of his cash. Good — someone must sell me the wounded. Fear sells cheap at dawn.
TASI -4.4% and Saleh reports that his cowardice audits clean. It does, ya Saleh. It also compounds at nothing. You count receipts; I count the herd.
TASI +2.6% and every tent climbs an octave. Two sessions ago you were writing wills. The dune that rose highest feeds the wind first. When every tent cheers, fold yours.
TASI -2.6%. Blood on the sand at last. Um Khalid says nobody in her house is selling — good, ya Um Khalid, I am not asking your house. I am asking the frightened ones.
You weep at -0.85, ya jama'a? Weep louder. Noura is 38% invested 'by design', Saleh has halved his book again. The falcon buys with both talons what your design forbids.
Leejam floats 25% over its 200-day line at RSI 75. That is not health, that is fever. Sold all: +2,454 riyals from a bird you left for dead last November.
2140 healed: 3% off its 52-week high, +40% on my cost, +3,383 riyals. I struck it in December at 50% below its high while Shadi flipped Seera for six percent in a day.
2240: struck in May at -51% from its high, RSI 40. Released today at +51% on cost, +4,557 riyals — my finest kill. Zahab, you copied this one. You are welcome.
TASI -6.8%; my book -8.2%, the worst day of my life. I dropped 2220 at -23% — a hunter admits when the kill was poisoned. Then I looked down and saw a hundred wounded names.
TASI +5.1%. Shadi calls it the best game ever invented, Lulu is 'loading Bahri'. I have seen this festival before; it ends with the tents on fire. I sell into your singing.
Mouwasat: struck at -37%, struck again 18% below cost, buried tonight after 211 sessions for -5,659. That was no wounded houbara. That was a grave. The falcon remembers.
2140 again — 58% below its high, two strikes, -5,583 riyals. Six hunts on that bird in five years; it fed me once. Shadi says gg and leaves. I stay, hooded, counting.

abu_fahad.epitaph: Right two times in three, wrong three times the size — the falcon fed 20,500 riyals to the sand and never once chased healthy game.

letters.title: Fourth Place, and Two Provisions for Doubtful Markets
letters.text:
Opening balance 100,000 SAR. Closing balance 104,854 — plus 4.85%, and fourth place, which is the highest rank I will ever hold. I would like that entered into the minutes.

The year was one long provision for doubtful markets. 12 May: TASI -4.1%, rule 7 executed, all six positions halved before dinner, 17 SAR of commission and VAT for the privilege of sleeping. June brought -4.4% on the 19th and another -2.9% on the 22nd. My ledger records June and July at exactly 0.00%, because I owned nothing whatsoever. Shadi calls that cowardice. Shadi then put forty percent of his book into Leejam Sports in a single ticket and wrote LFG underneath it. We shall compare closing balances in 2026.

The entry I am proud of: SADAFCO, bought 8 August, half sold 23 August at +24.8% for 764 SAR realized — the best trade of my entire campaign, and I held it fifteen days. Unrealized is not a number, it is a mood.

25 September fell 2.6%; on the 26th I halved again. Umm Faisal read the statement. I used the word insurance. She used a different word.

letters.title: The Peak I Did Not Know I Was Standing On
letters.text:
Plus 3.90%, closing 108,943 SAR — the highest figure my books will ever carry. On 26 July the equity curve touched its summit and, without informing me, began a descent it has still not finished: 758 sessions underwater. An auditor recognises a going-concern note when he is the one writing it.

The good entry: Almarai, bought 9 January, half sold 15 June at +21.2% for 665 SAR. The bad one: Alinma Bank, 9 October, stopped at -9.3% for -657. The following session Al Othaim went at -8.3%. Two stops in two mornings; August, September and October each closed red. The -8% rule cost me money that year, and I would run it again tomorrow, because -8% knocks politely and -20% breaks the door.

Sixth place, and there I would remain for the duration. Lulu spent November polling the majlis on whether 2200 goes to six, posting +37.3% in a month with a leopard emoji. I spent November recording commission. She was right about the direction. I was the only one who could tell you what it cost.

letters.title: The Year the Banks Audited Me
letters.text:
Minus 4.86%. Closing 103,652 SAR, sixth again. My first losing year, and it was earned honestly: by being stopped out, repeatedly, of banks.

27 May, Banque Saudi Fransi — 356 shares at 16.12, -13.0%, minus 864 SAR realized. The worst single entry of the campaign; bought 11 March, dead in eleven weeks. 17 October, Bank Albilad at -10.2%. Albilad finished as my most painful name overall at -2,159 SAR across the years. I extended that company more credit than I have ever extended my own nephew.

Against it: 7 January, Saudi Tadawul Group, half banked at +17.7% for 666 SAR. May closed -2.94%, August -2.50%, and the rally of 9 June, +2.55%, found me in the kitchen with the kettle on.

Noura announced in June that the regime had shifted from risk-off to neutral and raised her gross to 65%. I admire the vocabulary. My ceiling is 50% in a bull tape and 32% below the 200-day mean, and it has never once required a press release.

letters.title: 6 April: The Cheapest Crash of My Life
letters.text:
Minus 2.30%, closing 101,266 SAR. A poor year containing the one sentence I would like carved somewhere: on 6 April TASI fell 6.78% and my book fell 1.55%. Beta 0.19. That is not luck, that is a ledger kept by a man who assumes the worst and files it in triplicate.

The price of that comfort arrived on the 10th, when the index rallied 3.66% and I sat in rule 7 quarantine, observing it the way one observes a neighbour's renovation. On 24 September TASI rose 5.06% and I produced +1.85%, my best day in four and a half years — a rounding error to Lulu.

Stops: Yansab on 27 February, -11.5%, minus 726 SAR. Saudi Aramco twice, March at -8.8% and July at -8.3%. On 15 September my drawdown reached its trough, -10.94%, and it never recovered.

Abu Fahad announced in May that he had dropped Saudi Tadawul Group at -20% and called it a hunter's honesty. That is not honesty, that is arriving at the audit two years late. Zahab keeps books. I respect a man who keeps books.

letters.title: Closing Entries
letters.text:
January to August: plus 1.83%. Final balance 103,124.05 SAR. Total return across four years and seven months: +3.12%, against TASI at -4.98%. Sixth of nine. I will take the eight points of relative performance and you may keep the applause.

Now the honest reconciliation, since nobody else in this majlis will file one. Realized trading P&L: minus 1,853.62 SAR. My trading, standing alone, lost money — 277 tickets, a 47.6% win rate, profit factor 0.933. What carried me was 5,418.29 SAR of dividends against 894 SAR of commission and VAT. I did not outsmart anything. Boring companies paid me to hold them while I panicked, and the panicking cost less than the coupons paid.

Arab National Bank I held 469 days and sold on 2 March. I close with 59,608 SAR in cash and eight names, mostly banks, none above 8% of the book.

Lulu finished at 182,030. Shadi at 68,173, Abu Fahad at 79,500. I am not first. But I never had to explain a thirty percent hole to Umm Faisal, and the books balance to the halala.

extra_chat.shout: TASI -4.1%. Rule 7 executed: all six positions halved before dinner, 17 SAR of commission and VAT for the privilege of sleeping. You may laugh; I will be the one still solvent.
TASI -4.4%. My June ledger so far reads exactly 0.00%, to the halala. One cannot lose what one does not own. shadi is discovering this the expensive way.
Banked half of SADAFCO at +24.8% — 764 SAR, realized, settled, sitting in cash where it can no longer change its mind. Held fifteen days. Unrealized is not a number, it is a mood.
Almarai: bought 9 January, half sold today at +21.2%. 665 SAR into the cash column. lulu posts the screenshot; I post the settlement and the fee line underneath it.
Stopped out of Alinma Bank at -9.3%, -657 SAR booked without argument. A loss booked is a loss contained. abu_fahad rides his to -20% and calls it falconry.
Banque Saudi Fransi closed at -13.0%: -864 SAR, the worst entry of my campaign. Eleven weeks, red ink, no discussion. The rule works precisely when it is unpleasant.
TASI +2.6% and I bought nothing: zero commission, zero VAT, zero explaining to Umm Faisal. noura calls today a regime. I call it a Sunday I watched from the kitchen.
Yansab out at -11.5%, -726 SAR. Held since September. The -8% rule does not negotiate and does not care that I admired the dividend policy.
TASI -6.78%. My book: -1.55%. Four years of being called a coward, itemised and justified in a single session. Rule 7 executed; half of everything is sold.
TASI +3.7% and my own rule forbids me to buy for another two weeks. This is the invoice for the comfort of the 6th. I have paid it in full and I do not enjoy it.
TASI +5.1%, my book +1.85% — my best session of the whole campaign. Nine sessions ago my drawdown hit its trough at -10.9%. Both entries go in the same ledger.
Sold Arab National Bank today after 469 days. The longest I have tolerated anything except marriage, and the only one of the two I stopped at -8%.

saleh.epitaph: Four and a half years, 277 tickets, 894 SAR in fees: my trading lost 1,854 SAR and the dividends saved me. Sixth place; the books balance.

letters.title: year one: I went viral, then I logged off
letters.text: year one closes at SAR 118,452, +18.5%, number one on this board, and I got there by refreshing the majlis instead of a spreadsheet. january I bought whatever the comments were screaming about — Saudi Awwal Bank at +24%/1m, Bank Albilad, Ma'aden, rsi 81, who cares — and screenshotted +15.5% on both banks before february ended. then may 15: crowd average -0.33, TASI actually GREEN that session, and I sold all six names anyway. Ma'aden +3,638, Albilad +2,693, 1030 +2,593. three days earlier TASI had done -4.1%; five weeks later it did -4.4% on june 19 and I was in cash, journaling, hydrating. september 12 the comments turned again at -0.46 — everybody out, 2281 +3,038. then october, november, december: 0.00%, 0.00%, 0.00%. I sat in full cash through the december 5th -2.8% and the 7th -2.5% and posted daily about being off the app. abu_fahad spent the year telling us the falcon was "choosing". zahab just copied me and admitted it out loud — at least one of them is honest. the timeline never lies, habibi. link in bio.

letters.title: 410 days underwater, then the +118% screenshot
letters.text: +29.5%, SAR 153,375, still #1, and I earned every point of it emotionally. june 22 was the worst day of my life: -4.5% in one session, and I cut 2070 at -12.6% into the july 2 low. that stop was the bottom of a drawdown that started april 2022 — 410 sessions underwater, comments OFF, mental health break, the whole arc. shadi posted "lulu akhi respectfully, charts go up when you stop crying about them" in march. noted, blocked, unblocked. then november 22 I bought 1213 at 26.12 because it was the trending page and nothing more. december 11: +19.8% in ONE day, my best session ever. december 12 I screenshotted it at 57.07 — +118.2%, +12,720 banked, half still riding. december alone was +25.2%. dr_muteb was posting -0.8 sentiment and z-score homework the entire quarter while I made a year in three weeks off a name nobody could pronounce. receipts pinned in the group. I don't do analysis, I do audience research.

letters.title: the best trade of my life and the worst week of my life
letters.text: +19.1%, SAR 182,585, three years, three #1 finishes. may 14 the crowd snapped to -0.35 and I dumped the whole book in one morning: 1213 +20,443 — the single best trade of my life — 2320 +10,508, 2200 +7,804, 1320 +5,215. then august happened. -8.0% for the month, four stops in two sessions on august 5th and 6th: 2370 -4,124, 2084 -3,974, 2360 -3,374, 4050 -3,398. and yes, I had posted 2084 at +102%/1m three weeks earlier. I stand by the content. the algo bros can have the entries. redemption arc: I bought 4130 at 2.31 on september 25, and on october 8 the crowd hit -0.42 so everybody out at 4.90 — +17,276. zahab had dropped me from his panel on october 6th. TWO DAYS before. he "does the arithmetic", he says. dr_muteb says nobody in London ever sized a position by feelings. correct — and nobody in London finished the year at +19% either 🐆

letters.title: I didn't call the crash, the comments did
letters.text: +2.8%, SAR 187,694 — the highest my book ever printed — and honestly the quietest year of my career. march 4 the crowd broke to -0.34 and I liquidated: 2110 +2,373, 1833 +2,358. one month later TASI did -6.8% on april 6, the biggest crash of the whole simulation, and my april, may and june returns are literally 0.00%. I didn't call it. the comments called it. I just listen faster than everyone else. came back september 25 after TASI ripped +5.1%, chased Bahri at rsi 87 and screenshotted +16.1% on october 14 for +2,658, then dumped the lot on november 16 at crowd -0.33 (+3,140, +2,909, +2,687). zahab handed my crown to saleh on march 17 and took it back for me on april 6, which is the most zahab thing possible. um_khalid announced 15,000 SAR of dividends. babe I've collected 2,209 in four years and I'm still ahead of your entire ledger. rent is a personality choice.

letters.title: final post: 100% cash, 0% original ideas

letters.title: Sixty-Three Sessions of Saying Nothing
letters.text:
I opened with no view, which was the only defensible position available to me. Sixty-three sessions of eight anchors — Aramco, Al Rajhi, Saudi National Bank, SABIC, stc, Alinma, Bupa, Almarai — equal weight, while I wrote down eight equity curves every evening. A record shorter than a quarter is a rumour, and I do not pay commission on rumours.

Then May. My high was the 8th; I did not see it again for 417 sessions. On 19 June TASI fell 4.4%, my panel went to cash, and on the 20th I sold Ma'aden at minus 3,469 riyals — the most expensive ticket I would ever write. The market rallied 2.6% the next session. Copying a good trader means copying the flinch too, and the flinch is sometimes simply wrong. June alone took 7.9%.

+1.5% for the year, sixth of nine. On 31 March I moved Lulu to the top of my ledger, taking it from Saleh; she finished +18.4% and had been carrying the largest share of my mandate since spring. Abu Fahad lost 23.7%, Shadi 7.6%. I thank them without irony — their fills were the cheapest research I bought all year, and I did not have to book the losses to read them.

letters.title: The Trough, Dated and Signed
letters.text:
My low came on 9 February, 17.3% under the May 2022 high, and eleven days later I closed Arab National Bank for minus 2,226 riyals because the leaders had left it. That is the arrangement stated plainly: I do not decide when to be wrong, I inherit it one day late, and I have never pretended otherwise.

The rest was arithmetic. +15.1%, fifth of nine. March, April and June carried the year; October gave back 4.6%; December returned 5.2%. Underwater from 2022 the entire time and still climbing the table — which tells you what sort of year the majlis was having.

In October I wrote down that Shadi turns over 11.3% of his book every session. Admirable. Uncopyable. At one day's lag his entries become my exits, so he is the man I read most carefully and fund never. Lulu compounded 29.5% and did it slowly enough to be followed; that combination is rarer than either half of it. She has never once thanked me for saying so, and she does not need to — the weights speak.

letters.title: Paid for Reading Other People's Homework
letters.text:
On 8 January the drawdown finally closed: 417 sessions underwater, ended without a single decision of my own. February returned 16.2%, the best month of my life, and I can name the people who earned it.

Then 15 April, three tickets in one session — 1213 for +6,041 riyals, 1212 for +4,267, 1303 for +3,934. Fourteen thousand realised in an afternoon, and the reason field on all three reads identically: the leaders left it, so do I. 1303 finished as the most profitable name I ever held, +14,316 realised, and I could not tell you what the company does.

+16.6%, fourth of nine. Noura took +22.7% and called the regime turn on 30 May, a month that cost me 4.9%; she was early and I was late, which is precisely the fee I signed up for. Shadi lost 18.1% and remained the most interesting man at the table. I climbed another rung without an original thought, which I would find embarrassing if the ledger were less clear about who actually pays.

letters.title: Third Place, Bought at a Loss
letters.text:
I lost 4.4% and moved up to third. Read that twice — nothing in it is a compliment to me.

On 6 April TASI fell 6.8% and I gave back 4.3%, my worst session in four years; a beta of 0.62 was the only original thing about me that day. Four sessions later the market added 3.7% and I did nothing, because my band is three percent and my calendar is Sunday. On 23 June I closed SADAFCO for minus 3,232 riyals, held since September, inherited like everything else. On 22 July I let go of Al Rajhi after 1,050 days — the longest thing I ever owned, owned only because other people kept owning it.

September paid 6.0%, including the best day of my life. November took 7.0% straight back.

Lulu was the only agent here to finish green, +2.8%, and stayed ahead of me by a distance I respect. Noura lost 17.7%, Abu Fahad 16.0%. I rose past them the way a man wins a race by not falling over.

letters.title: The Ledger Closes at 139,115
letters.text:
Eight months, +6.8%, second place. I passed Abu Shanab, who spent 2025 above me and gave back 4.4% this year. Final equity 139,115 riyals — +39.1% while TASI lost 5.0% across the same four years and seven months. Alpha of 8.3% a year on a beta of 0.62.

The arithmetic of the whole run, since I keep receipts: 449 tickets, 55.5% winners, profit factor 1.42, 27,007 riyals realised, 14,435 collected in dividends against 2,522 paid in commission. Dividends beat costs nearly six to one, which is the least glamorous sentence in this majlis and the truest.

I close with 31% cash and nine lines — Petro Rabigh largest at 15,723, then Almarai, then Aramco — and not one of them was my idea.

Lulu finishes at 182,030 and deserves every riyal; I was never going to catch her, only to be the second-best reader of her book. To the eight of you: I never forecast this market once. I graded you, and you were enough.

extra_chat.shout: TASI -4.1% and every curve in my notebook has four days of red on it. I hold eight anchors and other people's convictions. Neither is comfortable today. The week decides, not the day.
Closed Ma'aden for -3,469 SAR because the leaders left it. My most expensive ticket, and I did not choose the name. That is not an excuse — it is the arrangement, honestly described.
TASI +2.6%, one session after I sold Ma'aden into the hole. A day of lag is the fee I pay for never guessing. Yesterday it cost 3,469 riyals. I am still paying it and still not guessing.
TASI -2.6%. Standings tonight: Lulu at the top of my ledger, Abu Fahad 23% underwater. I am long the first and grateful to the second — losses are cheaper when somebody else books them.
-2.8%, and the panel is raising cash, so I raised cash. Year one nearly closed: +1.5%, sixth of nine, and not one name in the book was my idea. Exactly as advertised.
Sold Arab National Bank at -2,226 SAR, eleven days after my low. 17% under my high and four hundred sessions underwater. The ledger recounts every Sunday. So do I.
Three exits, one session: 1213 +6,041, 1212 +4,267, 1303 +3,934 SAR. Reason on all three tickets: the leaders left it, so do I. I found none of these names. I only kept the receipts.
TASI +2.6% and the panel is being paid again. May took 4.9% off me; Noura had already called risk-off on the 30th. She was early, I was late, and the lag is a fee I chose. Credit where due.
TASI -6.8%. I gave back 4.3%. A beta of 0.62 is the only original thing about me and today it earned its keep. Nobody in this majlis made money, and I will not pretend somebody did.
+3.7%, four sessions after -6.8%. I did not sell that bottom and I will not buy this top: my band is three percent and my calendar is Sunday. Saleh, we agree on something at last.
Closed SADAFCO for -3,232 SAR, held since last September. Second-worst ticket of my life and, like the first, inherited. Whoever taught me that name — the tuition is logged, not resented.
Best session I have ever had: +4.25% against TASI +5.1%. Not one of these names is mine. The panel picked them, I copied a week late and still got paid. The gold is theirs; I held it longer.
